sub_tasks.requirements: The two-level progressive group quantization scheme (per-channel INT8 with protective range [-119, 119] followed by per-group INT4 with unsigned INT8 group scales) is correctly implemented so that dequantized intermediate weights stay within INT8 range for computation.
Level-1 per-channel symmetric INT8 weight quantization (Equation 4) is implemented.

Code has been implemented that takes a floating-point weight tensor W of shape (k, n) and computes per-output-channel FP16 scales s^(0) of shape (n, 1) using symmetric quantization (no zero point) as in Equation 4.

verification.spec: Locate the level-1 quantization function in QoQ. Feed a random weight tensor W of shape (k=1024, n=512) in FP32. Verify: (a) output s^(0) has shape (n, 1) and dtype float16, (b) s^(0)[j] == max(|W[:,j]|) / 119 (symmetric with protective range 119), (c) no zero points are produced. Confirm computation matches Equation 4 with protective range 119.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes the level-1 scale as s^(0) = max(|W_channel|) / 119 (using the protective range denominator 119) rather than the standard 127, on a per-channel basis.

verification.spec: Construct a random weight tensor W of shape [n, k]. Call the QoQ level-1 scale computation. Assert that for each channel i, the computed s^(0)_i equals max(|W[i,:]|) / 119 within 1e-6 relative tolerance, and NOT max(|W[i,:]|)/127.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that produces the intermediate signed 8-bit weight tensor QW^(0) = round(W / s^(0)) as an int8 tensor with the same shape as W.

verification.spec: Given W and s^(0) from level-1 quantization, verify that QW^(0) = round(W / s^(0)) is produced as an int8 tensor with the same shape as W and that all values lie in [-119, 119] (protective range). Test on a random W tensor and assert dtype==torch.int8 and value range.

sub_tasks.requirements: After level-1 quantization, all elements of QW^(0) lie within the protective range [-119, 119] (inclusive) for every channel, verified by asserting max(|QW^(0)|) <= 119.

verification.spec: Feed a set of random weight tensors (including tensors with extreme outliers) through the QoQ level-1 INT8 quantization step. Assert torch.max(torch.abs(QW0)) <= 119 for every case, and that the quantization does NOT use torch.clamp/saturation to enforce this (the scale itself must produce in-range values).

sub_tasks.requirements: Level-2 per-group asymmetric INT4 weight quantization on the INT8 intermediate weights (Equation 5) is implemented.
Code has been implemented that partitions QW^(0) along the input-channel dimension into groups of size g (default g=128) for level-2 quantization.

verification.spec: Call the level-2 quantization routine on an int8 QW^(0) tensor of shape (k=1024, n=512) with group size g=128. Verify that the input channel dimension k is partitioned into k/g=8 groups, and per-group scale/zero-point tensors have shape (n, k/g) = (512, 8). Confirm g defaults to 128.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes per-group asymmetric INT4 quantization parameters: an unsigned INT8 scale s^(1) = ceil((qmax - qmin)/(15 - 0)) and an unsigned INT4 zero point z per group from the min/max of QW^(0) in that group.

verification.spec: For a group of INT8 values from QW^(0), invoke the level-2 quantization routine. Assert s^(1) == ceil((qmax - qmin) / 15) as an unsigned INT8 (dtype uint8, value in [0,255]), and z == round(-qmin / s^(1) - qmin_signed) as unsigned INT4 (dtype uint8, value in [0,15]). Compare against a reference implementation on 20 random groups.

sub_tasks.requirements: The stored level-2 scales s^(1) have dtype unsigned INT8 (uint8) with shape (n, k/g), and the stored zero points z have dtype unsigned INT4 (packed or stored in uint8) with shape (n, k/g).

verification.spec: After running level-2 quantization with g=128, inspect the returned s^(1) and z tensors. Assert: s^(1).dtype == torch.uint8 and shape == (n, k/g); z tensor is stored as uint8 with values in [0, 15] (unsigned INT4 range) and shape == (n, k/g) (or packed equivalent halving one dimension). Verify on a random test tensor.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that produces the final unsigned INT4 quantized weight tensor QW = round(QW^(0)/s^(1) + z) clamped to [0, 15], with shape (n, k).

verification.spec: Import the QoQ quantization module and call the level-2 INT4 quantization function on a random FP16 weight tensor of shape (n=256, k=512) with group size 128. Assert that the returned QW tensor has dtype uint8 (or int8) with values strictly in [0, 15], shape (256, 512), and that the returned zero-points and scales tensors have shape (256, 512/128)=(256, 4).

sub_tasks.requirements: Protective range enforcement guarantees that INT4->INT8 dequantization produces values inside the INT8 range without saturation instructions.
The protective range constant 119 (derived from 127*15/16 as in Equation 6) is used explicitly in the level-1 quantization denominator and is documented in the code.

verification.spec: Grep the QoQ quantization source code for the literal constant 119 used in the level-1 (per-channel INT8) quantization denominator/clip range. Verify (a) the constant 119 appears in the level-1 quantization implementation, (b) there is an accompanying comment or docstring referencing the protective range and Equation 6 / value 127*15/16.

sub_tasks.requirements: For any input weight tensor, after performing level-1 and level-2 quantization followed by the level-2 dequantization (QW - z) * s^(1), every resulting intermediate value lies within [-128, 127] (INT8 range) without applying saturating arithmetic.

verification.spec: Run progressive group quantization (level-1 per-channel INT8 with protective range 119, then level-2 per-group asymmetric INT4) on 100 random weight tensors of shape [n,k]. For each, dequantize back to INT8 via (QW_u4 - z_u4) * s^(1)_u8 using pure integer arithmetic (no saturation). Assert every element of the intermediate result lies in [-128, 127].

sub_tasks.requirements: Saturating arithmetic instructions (e.g., sat variants) are NOT used in the dequantization path from INT4 to INT8; the implementation relies solely on the protective range to avoid overflow.

verification.spec: Search the INT4->INT8 dequantization CUDA/C++ kernels and Python code in the QServe repo for saturating arithmetic intrinsics (e.g., 'sat', '.sat', '__vaddss4', 'vaddss', 'saturate', 'clamp' in the dequant path). Assert none of these appear in the main-loop dequantization from UINT4 to SINT8, confirming reliance on the protective range.

sub_tasks.requirements: The dequantization pipeline from stored QoQ tensors back to floating point is implemented consistently with the two-level scheme.

verification.spec: Construct known QW_u4, z_u4 (in [0,15]) and s^(1)_u8 tensors. Call the level-2 dequantization function and verify the output equals (QW_u4 - z_u4) * s^(1)_u8 elementwise with per-group broadcasting. Also assert the output values all lie in the signed INT8 range [-128, 127].

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for level-1 dequantization multiplying the intermediate QW^(0)_hat by the per-channel FP16 scale s^(0) to recover the approximate FP16 weight.

verification.spec: Given a level-2-dequantized INT8 intermediate QW^(0)_hat and an FP16 per-channel scale s^(0), call the level-1 dequantization function and verify the output equals QW^(0)_hat.astype(fp16) * s^(0) broadcast across the input-channel dimension, matching a reference numpy/torch computation to within 1e-3 relative error.

sub_tasks.requirements: Round-trip quantize->dequantize on a random FP16 weight tensor recovers a tensor whose per-element error is bounded by the theoretical two-level quantization error (max |W - W_hat| <= s^(0) * s^(1) / 2 per group).

verification.spec: Generate a random FP16 weight tensor W of shape (256, 512). Run progressive-group-quantize then progressive-dequantize with group size 128 to obtain W_hat. Assert max |W - W_hat| <= (s^(0) * s^(1))/2 elementwise per group (with a small tolerance for FP16 rounding). Additionally check per-group MSE decreases as group size decreases.

sub_tasks.requirements: The QoQ scheme is distinguished from prior VSQuant/DoubleQuant/DGQ two-level quantization approaches.

verification.spec: Read the progressive quantization function source. Verify that in the call sequence, the input FP16 W is first passed through the per-channel INT8 quantize step producing an INT8 intermediate, and only then the INT8 intermediate is passed to the per-group INT4 quantize step. Additionally verify by monkey-patching/tracing that a call graph on a test tensor invokes int8_quant before int4_group_quant.

sub_tasks.requirements: The level-2 scales are stored as unsigned INT8 (not FP16), enabling INT8-only arithmetic during GEMM dequantization, matching the QoQ design and distinguishing it from FP16-scale approaches.

verification.spec: Quantize a random FP16 weight tensor with the QoQ progressive quantizer. Inspect the returned level-2 scale tensor and assert its dtype is uint8 (torch.uint8 or numpy.uint8) and all values are in [0, 255]. Assert it is NOT a floating-point dtype.

verification.spec: For a head with head_dim D (e.g., D=128), compute the SmoothAttention lambda vector. Assert that for every i in [0, D/2), lambda[i] == lambda[i + D/2] exactly. Test with several D values (64, 128, 256).

sub_tasks.requirements: The paired scale is computed by aggregating the per-channel statistics across the two paired channels (i and i+D/2) before taking the alpha-power, so the resulting scale respects the RoPE rotation of channel pairs.

verification.spec: Inspect the scale-computation routine: verify that the per-channel stat used for channel i is aggregated (max, mean, or the paper's specific combine) with the stat for channel i+D/2 BEFORE the alpha-power is applied, and that the resulting scale satisfies lambda[i] == lambda[i+D/2] exactly. Test on a random stats vector.

sub_tasks.requirements: A behavioral check verifies that applying SmoothAttention scaling before RoPE and after RoPE produces mathematically equivalent Query/Key outputs (within floating-point tolerance), confirming the RoPE-commutativity constraint is correctly implemented.

verification.spec: Construct a random Q and K tensor of shape (batch, num_heads, seq, head_dim). Apply RoPE then SmoothAttention scaling, and separately apply SmoothAttention scaling then RoPE (with lambda[i]==lambda[i+D/2] constraint). Assert the two results are elementwise equal within 1e-3 relative FP16 tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: SmoothAttention scales are applied to Queries and Keys with inverse relationship such that Q K^T remains mathematically equivalent to the original.
Code has been implemented that divides Keys by the per-channel Lambda (K -> Lambda^{-1} K), migrating outlier magnitudes out of the KV cache prior to quantization.

verification.spec: In a pre-fusion mode (before absorbing into W_K), run the SmoothAttention transform on a random K tensor and assert the returned K' equals K / Lambda broadcasted per-channel, and that column-wise max of |K'| is lower than that of |K| on channels where lambda>1.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that multiplies Queries by the same per-channel Lambda (Q -> Q Lambda), so that (Q Lambda)(Lambda^{-1} K)^T = Q K^T is preserved.

verification.spec: In pre-fusion mode, run the SmoothAttention transform on a random Q tensor and assert Q' == Q * Lambda broadcasted per-channel. Then compute (Q*Lambda)(K/Lambda)^T and compare to Q K^T; assert equality within 1e-3 relative FP16 tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: A behavioral test verifies that attention scores computed with SmoothAttention applied (before quantization) match the original attention scores within floating-point tolerance on a small input.

verification.spec: Build a small attention layer with random Q, K, V and RoPE. Compute attention output O_ref. Then apply SmoothAttention by fusing Lambda into W_Q and Lambda^-1 into W_K (with the paired-channel constraint from Eq. 10). Recompute attention output O_smooth. Assert torch.allclose(O_ref, O_smooth, atol=1e-4, rtol=1e-4).

sub_tasks.requirements: SmoothAttention scaling is fused into the weights of the preceding QKV projection, eliminating any extra kernel/scaling call at runtime.
Code has been implemented that fuses the SmoothAttention scale into W_Q by setting W_Q <- Lambda W_Q (absorbing the per-output-channel scale into the Query projection weights).

verification.spec: Given original W_Q of shape (H*D, hidden) and a per-head Lambda vector of shape (H, D), apply the fusion function and assert that the returned W_Q_fused equals diag(Lambda_flat) @ W_Q (i.e., each output row i is scaled by Lambda[i//D, i%D]). Verify numerically on a random small tensor.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that fuses the inverse SmoothAttention scale into W_K by setting W_K <- Lambda^{-1} W_K, so that no runtime scaling of K is required.

verification.spec: Given original W_K of shape (H_kv*D, hidden) and a Lambda vector, apply the fusion function and assert that W_K_fused equals diag(1/Lambda_flat) @ W_K. Verify numerically on a random small tensor.

sub_tasks.requirements: After fusion, the runtime attention/KV path contains no explicit SmoothAttention scaling kernel or elementwise multiply on Q/K activations, confirming zero runtime overhead as claimed in the paper.

verification.spec: Instrument or grep the QServe attention forward path for any per-channel multiplicative scaling of Q or K activations attributed to SmoothAttention (e.g., a 'smooth_scale' multiply between qkv_proj and RoPE/attention). Assert no such runtime kernel exists in the fused model — only W_Q and W_K weight fusion. Additionally run a forward pass with a profiler and verify no kernel named/tagged with 'smooth' executes in the attention block.

sub_tasks.requirements: The SmoothAttention fusion correctly handles grouped-query attention (GQA) models by broadcasting/aligning the K-side scale across the query heads that share each KV head.

verification.spec: Load a GQA model (e.g., Llama-3-8B with 32 Q heads / 8 KV heads). Compute SmoothAttention scales and fuse into W_Q and W_K. Verify: (a) the K-side scale for each KV head is applied to W_K rows corresponding to that KV head, and (b) the same per-KV-head scale is broadcast to the 4 Q heads sharing that KV head when fusing into W_Q. Confirm end-to-end forward output on random input matches an unfused reference within 1e-2 FP16 tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: SmoothAttention delivers the reported perplexity improvement on the KV4 quantized Llama-2-7B ablation.

Enabling SmoothAttention on top of the +4-bit KV Quant (W4A8KV4) configuration for Llama-2-7B reduces WikiText2 perplexity from 5.80 to 5.75 (an improvement of ~0.05), matching the ablation in Figure 16.

verification.spec: Quantize Llama-2-7B with QoQ W4A8KV4 (g128) in two configurations: (a) with 4-bit KV quantization but WITHOUT SmoothAttention, (b) same but WITH SmoothAttention (alpha=0.5). Evaluate WikiText2 perplexity at seq_len=2048 for both. Assert configuration (b) yields perplexity ~5.75 (within tolerance) and that (a) - (b) >= 0.03.

sub_tasks.requirements: Block input module rotation via scaled Hadamard, block output module smoothing (with migration strength near 0), activation-aware channel reordering, and block-MSE-based weight clipping (with special handling for q_proj/k_proj) are implemented.
Block input module rotation using a scaled Hadamard rotation matrix is applied to the block input activations (QKV projection input, FFN 1st layer input) and absorbed into preceding module weights.
Code has been implemented that constructs a scaled Hadamard rotation matrix Q of appropriate dimensions (matching the block input hidden size), such that Q Q^T = I.

verification.spec: Invoke the scaled-Hadamard construction routine for hidden sizes commonly used by target LLMs (4096, 5120, 8192). Assert (a) the returned Q has the requested shape, (b) torch.allclose(Q @ Q.T, torch.eye(n), atol=1e-5), and (c) each entry has magnitude 1/sqrt(n) as expected from a scaled Hadamard.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that identifies the block input modules (QKV projection, FFN gate/up projections following the block's input RMSNorm) and multiplies their weight matrices by Q on the input-channel side so that XW^T becomes (XQ)(Q^T W^T).

verification.spec: Inspect the block-rotation implementation: identify input modules (q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, gate_proj, up_proj) after the block's input RMSNorm. Verify each such module's weight W is replaced by W @ Q (or equivalently Q^T @ W^T for the transposed matmul), where Q is the Hadamard rotation matrix. Test on random input X: assert that XW^T equals (X Q)(Q^T W^T) within 1e-3 FP16 tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that fuses the rotation matrix Q into the weights of the previous block's output module (e.g., previous attention out_proj or FFN down_proj) so the rotation is not applied as a runtime kernel.

verification.spec: Inspect the quantization pipeline code (e.g., deepcompressor or QoQ preprocessing module) to confirm a function exists that fuses the rotation matrix Q into the previous block's output-module weights (attention out_proj or FFN down_proj). Verify by loading a small model, applying rotation fusion, and checking that the previous block's weight tensor has been updated (weights differ from original) while no separate rotation kernel/module is inserted in the forward graph.

sub_tasks.requirements: The rotation transformation preserves the mathematical output of the linear layer (verified numerically to within floating point tolerance on a sample input tensor).

verification.spec: Construct a small linear layer with random weights, generate a random input tensor, compute the reference output y_ref = X @ W^T. Apply the rotation transformation (rotate X by Q^T and W by Q), compute y_rot = (X Q^T) @ (W Q)^T, and assert torch.allclose(y_ref, y_rot, atol=1e-4, rtol=1e-4).

sub_tasks.requirements: Applying block input rotation demonstrably reduces the magnitude of activation outlier channels at the QKV/FFN1 inputs (post-rotation per-channel max is lower than pre-rotation on a calibration batch).

verification.spec: Load a small pretrained LLM block, run a calibration batch through it and capture per-channel max magnitudes of activations at the QKV projection and FFN1 input BEFORE rotation. Apply the block-input rotation transformation, rerun the calibration batch, capture the post-rotation per-channel max magnitudes. Assert that the maximum per-channel magnitude after rotation is strictly less than before (outlier suppression).

sub_tasks.requirements: Block output module smoothing with a diagonal per-channel scale Lambda is applied to the intermediate activations feeding the block output modules (attention out_proj, FFN down_proj) and fused into preceding weights.

Code has been implemented that computes a per-channel smoothing scale vector lambda for each block output module using a migration-strength formulation similar to SmoothQuant (function of activation and weight max magnitudes).

verification.spec: Locate the function in the quantization pipeline that computes per-channel smoothing factors for block output modules (e.g., attention out_proj, FFN down_proj). Verify the formula matches SmoothQuant-style migration: lambda_i = max(|X_i|)^alpha / max(|W_:,i|)^(1-alpha) with configurable alpha. Call the function on a synthetic activation/weight pair and confirm it returns a per-channel vector with expected shape and values.

sub_tasks.requirements: The migration strength alpha used for block output module smoothing is configured to a value near 0 (so lambda is determined mostly by weights rather than activations), distinct from the input-module smoothing regime.

verification.spec: Inspect the QoQ configuration (config file, default arg, or code constant) applied to block output modules (out_proj, down_proj) and confirm that the migration-strength alpha is set near 0 (e.g., alpha <= 0.1) and is distinct from the alpha used for input-module smoothing. Grep the codebase or load the config and assert the value.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that divides intermediate activations by Lambda and multiplies the output module weights by Lambda (W_out = W_out * Lambda) to preserve mathematical equivalence.

verification.spec: Create a small linear layer W and random input X. Compute y_ref = act_fn(X) @ W^T. Apply smoothing: X_smooth = act_fn(X) / Lambda, W_smooth = W * Lambda (broadcast on the input-channel dim). Compute y_smooth = X_smooth @ W_smooth^T and assert torch.allclose(y_ref, y_smooth, atol=1e-4).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that fuses the inverse smoothing scale Lambda^{-1} into the preceding modules (e.g., attention v_proj weights, FFN up_proj weights) so that no runtime smoothing kernel is required.

verification.spec: Inspect the quantization pipeline to confirm the smoothing scales Lambda^-1 are fused into preceding modules (v_proj, up_proj). Load a small model, apply smoothing fusion, and verify: (a) the preceding module weights have been modified (differ from original), (b) the forward graph does not contain a runtime division/scaling op for smoothing.

sub_tasks.requirements: Using migration strength equal to that of the input modules (rather than near 0) for output-module smoothing degrades Llama-2-7B WikiText2 perplexity by approximately the amount reported (~0.05), confirming the near-0 choice.

verification.spec: Quantize Llama-2-7B with QoQ using (a) output-module smoothing with migration strength near 0 (paper's chosen setting), and (b) output-module smoothing with the same migration strength used for input modules. Evaluate WikiText2 perplexity at seq_len=2048 for both. Assert perplexity(b) - perplexity(a) is approximately 0.05 (within tolerance 0.03).

sub_tasks.requirements: Activation-aware channel reordering groups weight input channels of similar salience (based on activation max magnitude) into the same quantization group.
Code has been implemented that computes a per-input-channel salience score using max(|X|) over a calibration set of activations for each linear layer subject to group quantization.

verification.spec: Locate the salience-computation function; feed it a synthetic calibration activation tensor of shape (N_calib, in_channels) with known per-channel maxima. Assert that the returned salience vector equals max(|X|) along the token dimension (or matches an equivalent per-channel absmax reduction over the calibration set).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that produces a channel permutation (e.g., via argsort of the salience vector) so that channels with similar salience end up within the same size-g quantization group.

verification.spec: Call the channel-reordering permutation function on a synthetic salience vector with distinct values. Verify that (a) the returned permutation is a valid permutation of range(in_channels), (b) after permuting and grouping into size-g contiguous blocks, the per-group variance of salience is lower than in the original ordering (channels with similar salience cluster in the same group). Reference implementation: perm = argsort(salience).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that permutes weight input channels and the corresponding activation channels consistently, and fuses the permutation into the preceding operator's output ordering so no runtime shuffle kernel is required.

verification.spec: Inspect the pipeline that applies channel reordering. Confirm: (a) weight input-channel permutation is applied to W (weight.shape unchanged, weights differ from original), (b) the same permutation is fused into the preceding operator's output ordering (e.g., preceding linear's out_channels reordered, or LayerNorm scale reordered) rather than an explicit runtime gather/shuffle in the forward pass. Grep forward code to confirm absence of runtime permutation ops on activations.

sub_tasks.requirements: The reordering transformation preserves the output of the linear layer (matmul on a sample input yields numerically identical results before and after reordering, within floating point tolerance).

verification.spec: Construct a random linear layer W and input X. Compute y_ref = X @ W^T. Generate a random permutation perm; compute X_p = X[:, perm], W_p = W[:, perm]; compute y_perm = X_p @ W_p^T. Assert torch.allclose(y_ref, y_perm, atol=1e-5). This validates the permutation preserves matmul output.

sub_tasks.requirements: Block-MSE-based weight clipping determines per-layer clip ratios by minimizing an output MSE objective, using layer output MSE for most linear layers and block output MSE specifically for q_proj and k_proj.
Code has been implemented that grid-searches a clip ratio alpha in [0,1] to shrink the weight dynamic range (W_max = alpha * max(W), W_min = alpha * min(W)) before quantization.

verification.spec: Instantiate the QoQ clipping search on a random linear layer with a fixed calibration batch. Assert that (a) the searched alpha lies in [0,1], (b) the routine evaluates multiple candidate alphas (>= 5 distinct values), and (c) the selected alpha minimizes the objective across the candidates. Verify W_max = alpha*max(W) and W_min = alpha*min(W) are used to compute the scale/zero.

sub_tasks.requirements: For linear layers other than q_proj and k_proj, the clip-ratio search objective minimizes the per-layer output MSE ||XW^T - X Q(W;alpha)^T||.

verification.spec: Locate the clip-ratio search routine in the QoQ quantization code. Verify that for linear layers other than q_proj and k_proj, the objective evaluated in the alpha grid search is the per-layer output MSE ||X @ W^T - X @ Q(W;alpha)^T||_2, and NOT the weight-only error ||W - Q(W;alpha)||. Confirm by inspecting the loss function passed to the search and by running the search on a small layer.

sub_tasks.requirements: For q_proj and k_proj specifically, the clip-ratio search objective minimizes the block output MSE (measured at the output of the transformer block or attention block) rather than the per-layer output MSE, per Equation 11.

verification.spec: Inspect the QoQ clipping routine invocation on q_proj and k_proj vs. other linear layers (e.g., o_proj, gate_proj). Assert the objective function used for q_proj/k_proj is computed at the transformer/attention block output (not the per-layer output), while other linears use per-layer output MSE. Verify by patching the objective and confirming which activations are read.

sub_tasks.requirements: The weight clipping procedure operates on the intermediate 8-bit (progressive quantization stage-0) weights or the final quantized weights consistently with the QoQ progressive group quantization pipeline.

verification.spec: Trace the quantization pipeline order: verify that weight clipping is applied consistently within the progressive group quantization flow (either on the stage-0 INT8 intermediates or on final quantized weights, in a documented manner). Inspect the code path from FP16 weights -> clipping -> stage-0 INT8 quant -> stage-1 INT4 quant, and confirm clipping occurs at the documented stage without breaking the progressive-quantization invariant (dequantized intermediates stay in [-119,119]).

sub_tasks.requirements: Adding block-MSE-based weight clipping on top of block input rotation improves Llama-2-7B WikiText2 perplexity by approximately the amount reported in the ablation (~0.16 improvement over the +rotation configuration).

verification.spec: Quantize Llama-2-7B W4A8KV4 with (a) block input rotation only, and (b) block input rotation + block-MSE-based weight clipping. Evaluate WikiText2 perplexity at seq_len=2048. Assert perplexity(a) - perplexity(b) is approximately 0.16 (within tolerance 0.05).

sub_tasks.requirements: The general quantization optimizations are integrated as a coherent calibration pipeline invoked prior to QoQ progressive group quantization.

Code has been implemented that runs the four optimizations (block input rotation, block output smoothing, activation-aware channel reordering, weight clipping) in a documented order over a calibration dataset and produces a modified model ready for W4A8KV4 quantization.

verification.spec: Run the QoQ preprocessing pipeline end-to-end on a small model (e.g., a tiny Llama variant or a single transformer block) with a small calibration set. Verify the four transformations are applied in a documented order (e.g., rotation -> smoothing -> reordering -> clipping) by logging or inspecting pipeline stages. Confirm the output is a transformed model checkpoint ready for W4A8KV4 quantization (contains modified weights and metadata such as scales/permutations).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that supports a calibration data loader (e.g., Pile or WikiText2 samples) used to compute activation statistics required by rotation-fusion, smoothing scales, channel salience, and clip-ratio search.

verification.spec: Verify the codebase contains a calibration data loader supporting datasets such as Pile or WikiText2 (grep for 'pile' or 'wikitext' in the calibration module). Instantiate the loader with a small sample count and confirm it yields tokenized batches. Confirm the loader is consumed by the rotation, smoothing, reordering, and clip-search routines (e.g., passed as an argument or via a shared config).

sub_tasks.requirements: The resulting transformed model, when saved and re-loaded for FP16 inference, produces outputs mathematically equivalent to the original model up to floating point rounding on a sample prompt.

verification.spec: Load a small pretrained LLM in FP16, run a sample prompt to record reference logits y_ref. Apply the full QoQ preprocessing pipeline (rotation+smoothing+reordering+clipping fusions, but NO quantization applied yet - keep FP16). Save and reload the transformed model. Run the same prompt and record y_transformed. Assert torch.allclose(y_ref, y_transformed, atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-2) - equivalence up to floating-point rounding through fused rotations/smoothings.

sub_tasks.requirements: The W4A8 GEMM kernel with compute-aware weight reordering, subtraction-after-multiplication computation order, register-level parallelism for UINT4->UINT8 unpacking, and epilogue-fused zero-point correction is implemented and achieves the intended speedup over cuBLAS W8A8.
The W4A8 GEMM kernel is implemented with the required data flow: INT4 weights + INT8 activations produce FP16 outputs via INT8 tensor cores with epilogue-fused first-level FP16 scaling.

Code has been implemented that provides a CUDA/PTX W4A8 GEMM kernel entry point (e.g., a callable function in QServe's kernel library) which accepts INT4-packed weights, INT8 activations, per-channel FP16 weight scales, FP16 activation scales, and (for per-group variant) INT8 second-level scales and UINT4 zero points, and returns FP16 output.

verification.spec: Import QServe's kernel module and locate the W4A8 GEMM entry point (e.g., qserve_backend.w4a8_gemm or equivalent). Using `inspect.signature`, assert its parameters accept: (a) INT4-packed weights (int8/uint8 tensor with packed dim), (b) INT8 activations, (c) FP16 per-channel weight scales, (d) FP16 activation scales, and (e) for the per-group variant, INT8 s^(1) and INT4 zero points. Call it on tiny random inputs and confirm it returns an FP16 tensor of the correct shape without error.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the W4A8 GEMM main loop performs its matrix-multiply-accumulate using INT8 tensor core mma instructions (mma.sync m16n8k32 or equivalent) rather than FP16/FP32 tensor cores.

verification.spec: Dump the SASS/PTX of the compiled QServe W4A8 GEMM kernel via `cuobjdump --dump-sass` (or `nvcc --ptx` at build). Assert the main loop contains INT8 `mma.sync.aligned.m16n8k32.row.col.s32.s8.s8.s32` instructions (or equivalent HMMA.16816.S8 SASS). Assert no HMMA.*.F16 (FP16 tensor core) instructions appear inside the main loop.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that fuses the first-level FP16 weight scaling (sW) and activation scaling (sX) as an outer-product scaling applied to INT32 accumulator results in the GEMM epilogue, producing FP16 outputs, so that per-channel scales never appear in the sequential main loop.

verification.spec: Locate the W4A8 GEMM kernel and confirm that per-channel FP16 weight scales sW and per-token activation scales sX are applied only in the epilogue as an outer-product scaling on the INT32 accumulator. Grep the CUDA source for the main-loop body (mma.sync loop) and verify no FP16 multiplies against sW/sX appear inside it; verify the epilogue produces FP16 outputs. Run the GEMM on random INT4 weights and INT8 activations with known scales and check that output equals (QX @ QW.T) * (sX outer sW) within FP16 tolerance (rtol=1e-2).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that provides both a per-channel W4A8 GEMM variant (no second-level scales) and a per-group W4A8 GEMM variant with group size 128 (with UINT8 second-level scales s(1) and UINT4 zero points z(1) per group).

verification.spec: Import the QServe GEMM module and verify that two distinct callable W4A8 GEMM entry points exist: a per-channel variant (no level-2 scales) and a per-group variant that accepts UINT8 level-2 scales and UINT4 zero points with group size 128. Confirm both variants can be invoked with appropriately shaped tensors without error and produce FP16 outputs.

sub_tasks.requirements: Compute-aware offline weight reordering that stores weights in the exact order consumed by INT8 tensor core threads is implemented, eliminating pointer-arithmetic overhead and enabling 128-bit packed loads.

Code has been implemented that provides an offline (checkpoint-preparation) utility which permutes INT4 weight tensors into the QServe compute-aware layout, and is invoked once when loading a QoQ-quantized model into QServe.

verification.spec: Locate the offline checkpoint-preparation utility in QServe (e.g., a weight-packing script or a load-time transform). Confirm it applies the compute-aware reorder (Figure 12c) to INT4 weight tensors: divides into 32x32 tiles, packs thread-major within each tile. Invoke it on a small dummy INT4 weight tensor and verify the output layout matches the documented pattern. Confirm this occurs once at load time, not per forward pass.

sub_tasks.requirements: The reordering divides the weight matrix into 32x32 tiles and, within each tile, concatenates the 32 input channels consumed by each thread (e.g., thread 0's input channels 0-3 and 16-19 across output channels 0, 8, 16, 24) into a single contiguous 128-bit word, with thread i+1's 128-bit word stored immediately after thread i's, matching Figure 12c.

verification.spec: Given a plain [n, k] INT4 weight matrix, invoke QServe's compute-aware weight reorder routine. Assert the output layout groups every 32x32 tile such that thread 0's 32 consumed input channels (0-3 and 16-19 across output channels 0, 8, 16, 24) form a contiguous 128-bit word, and thread 1's 128-bit word immediately follows thread 0's. Verify by reconstructing the original matrix from the reordered layout via the known thread mapping and comparing element-wise to the input.

sub_tasks.requirements: The reordering utility also permutes per-channel weight scales, per-group second-level scales, and per-group zero points into a matching layout so that they can be loaded alongside weights without additional pointer arithmetic.

verification.spec: Inspect the reordering utility to confirm it also permutes: (a) per-channel FP16 scales sW, (b) per-group UINT8 second-level scales sW^(1), (c) per-group UINT4 zero points zW, into a layout matching the reordered weights. Run the utility on a dummy quantized layer and verify scales/zeros shapes/strides align with weight tiles for direct load in the GEMM main loop without extra address arithmetic.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that the W4A8 GEMM kernel loads reordered weights from global memory using 128-bit per-thread transactions (e.g., cp.async.cg.shared.global with 16-byte granularity or LDG.128), rather than issuing narrower strided loads.

verification.spec: Inspect the QServe W4A8 GEMM kernel source (CUDA .cu file). Grep for 128-bit load instructions: 'cp.async.cg.shared.global' with 16-byte size or 'ldg.128' / '__ldg' with int4/uint4 vector types, or 'reinterpret_cast<int4*>' loads. Confirm the weight-loading path uses 128-bit-per-thread transactions and not narrower 32/64-bit strided loads.

sub_tasks.requirements: The kernel does not rely on ldmatrix for INT4 weight distribution (which would produce the storage-compute mismatch shown in Figure 12b), and instead each thread directly receives the exact tiles it needs for the subsequent INT8 mma call from the reordered layout.

verification.spec: Grep the QServe W4A8 GEMM kernel source for 'ldmatrix' usage on INT4 weight loads. Confirm that ldmatrix is NOT used for the packed INT4 weight tensor (it may still be used for INT8 activations). Confirm that the reordered layout places each thread's required tiles contiguously so a plain 128-bit LDG suffices, then mma.sync.aligned.m16n8k32.s8.s8 is called directly.

sub_tasks.requirements: The reordered weights, when consumed by the QServe W4A8 kernel, produce numerically equivalent results to a reference (non-reordered) W4A8 matmul on random test inputs (up to expected INT8 arithmetic equivalence).

verification.spec: Generate random INT4 weights and INT8 activations for a small M,N,K problem. Compute a reference W4A8 matmul using naive PyTorch (dequantize INT4 to INT8, then int matmul). Apply QServe's offline reordering to weights/scales/zeros, invoke the QServe W4A8 GEMM kernel, and assert the FP16 output matches the reference within INT8-arithmetic-equivalent tolerance (atol=1e-2 on FP16 output).

sub_tasks.requirements: Register-level parallel UINT4->UINT8 unpacking with a 3-logical-op path per group of four INT4 weights is implemented, exploiting the (w0, w16, w1, w17, ...) interleaving.

The offline weight-packing routine packs every 32 UINT4 weights into a 128-bit word using the interleave order w0, w16, w1, w17, w2, w18, ..., w15, w31 (as depicted in Figure 13) rather than the naive w0..w31 order.

verification.spec: Feed the offline weight-packing routine a known sequence of 32 UINT4 values [w0, w1, ..., w31]. Read back the packed 128-bit word and unpack the nibbles in the order they appear. Assert the packed nibble order equals [w0, w16, w1, w17, w2, w18, ..., w15, w31] (interleaved lower/upper halves), matching Figure 13, and NOT the naive [w0, w1, ..., w31].

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that UINT4->UINT8 unpacking for one group of packed weights uses at most three logical operations (e.g., AND with 0x0F0F0F0F mask, shift right by 4, and second AND/OR) per 4-way byte lane, matching the register-level-parallelism scheme described for Figure 13.

verification.spec: Inspect the CUDA source of the QServe W4A8 kernel's UINT4->UINT8 unpacking inline function. Count logical operations per 4-way byte lane produced from one 32-bit register holding 8 packed nibbles: expect at most 3 operations (e.g., an AND with 0x0F0F0F0F for the low nibbles, a shift-right by 4, and an AND or OR for the high nibbles). Confirm this pattern is present (e.g., via PTX/SASS inspection or source grep for 'and.b32' / 'shr.b32' / 'lop3').

sub_tasks.requirements: The unpacking step produces four UINT8 values packed into a 32-bit register (one per byte lane) suitable for direct consumption by subsequent vadd4 / mul / mma instructions without further shuffling.

verification.spec: Invoke (or reproduce via a host-side simulation) the unpacking step on a known input register value and verify the output is a 32-bit register whose four bytes each contain one UINT8 in [0,15], directly consumable by vadd4/mul without additional pack/shuffle instructions. Confirm no subsequent __byte_perm or shuffle appears between unpack and vadd4/mma in the kernel source.

sub_tasks.requirements: Per-channel W4A8 GEMM performs zero-point subtraction after multiplication by fusing (sW * sX) * (tX outer zW) correction into the epilogue, using a precomputed per-token tX = X * 1_k vector.
